issues.legal_issue: Landowners who agreed to compensation before a later differential ex gratia payment was introduced do not waive their right to challenge the resulting discrimination or seek revised compensation.

Differential compensation based on whether landowners are classified as ancestral or non-ancestral violates Article 14 when the classification lacks adequate evidentiary support, a rational nexus to its rehabilitation objective, and safeguards against arbitrary effects.

Classifying landowners for differential compensation according to the nature or duration of their ownership contravenes the Land Acquisition Act and the principle that compensation cannot vary by the type of owner when land is acquired for the same public purpose.
